qa.question: Should Bluegrass capacity stay at 208 MW per unit or follow EIA at 193.8 MW?
qa.finding: The draft Title V permit (https://dep.gateway.ky.gov/eSearch.WebApi/api/documentGenerate/getDocument/14642064) says each turbine can generate 208 MW. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists 193.8 MW nameplate for each of CT1, CT2 and CT3.
qa.recommendation: Change Capacity (MW) to 193.8 for each of the three units, since the EIA figure is the only one labeled as nameplate. If the reviewer prefers the permit rating, leave 208 MW as is.
qa.note: I searched for the reason for the gap. The Kentucky Division for Air Quality draft Title V permit (https://dep.gateway.ky.gov/eSearch.WebApi/api/documentGenerate/getDocument/14642064) gives a maximum continuous rating of 208 MW per turbine at the permit's rated heat input. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives a nameplate of 193.8 MW, a summer net of 165 MW and a winter net of 192 MW per unit. The Kentucky Public Service Commission staff report on the East Kentucky Power Cooperative 2025 resource plan (https://psc.ky.gov/pscscf/2025%20Cases/2025-00087//20260601_PSC_ORDER.pdf) gives 167 MW summer and 189 MW winter per turbine. No document I found gives a generator nameplate plate figure of 208 MW. The 208 MW figure is a permit rating, so it may be a maximum rather than the nameplate. EIA is the only source that labels its figure as nameplate.

source_log.note: Read the Operating sheet rows for plant 55164.
Statement of basis for permit V-21-048 R1 draft.
Draft permit V-21-048 R1 lists three 208 MW turbines, Siemens-Westinghouse 501FD.
Commission staff report in the 2025 resource plan case. It names the plant, says three turbines began commercial service in 2002, and gives 167 MW summer and 189 MW winter each.
The final order in the 2025 resource plan case. It does not name Bluegrass. It only sets the next plan due date of April 1, 2028.

The case 2025-00087 list shows no new unit, retirement or capacity change for Bluegrass. The resource plan lists three turbines totaling 501 MW summer and 567 MW winter, retrofitted for fuel oil in 2020, with no retirement planned.
